title: Wheat symptoms: celiac disease, allergy or sensitivity?
intro: Symptoms after wheat do not all have the same cause. Celiac disease is an immune reaction to gluten that damages the small bowel; wheat allergy and non-celiac sensitivity need different investigations and care.

sections.heading: Understanding the problem
paragraphs: Celiac disease may cause diarrhea, bloating, anemia or few digestive symptoms. Wheat allergy can cause rapid hives, swelling or breathing problems. Sensitivity is considered after other causes are excluded.

sections.heading: Assessment and tests
paragraphs: Do not start a gluten-free diet before discussing celiac testing, because avoidance can make results misleading. If wheat caused a suspected allergic reaction, do not challenge yourself at home; seek specialist advice. Bring your medicine list and previous results; ask which findings would change the plan.

sections.heading: Treatment choices
paragraphs: Confirmed celiac disease requires lifelong gluten avoidance and nutritional follow-up. Wheat allergy needs individualized avoidance and an emergency plan. Non-celiac sensitivity does not automatically require the same strict lifelong restrictions. Agree how benefit and adverse effects will be checked before changing treatment.

sections.heading: Everyday care
paragraphs: A dietitian can help preserve fiber, iron and other nutrients and explain label reading and cross-contact. Expensive commercial intolerance panels cannot establish these diagnoses or justify eliminating many foods. Choose a routine you can maintain, and discuss barriers such as cost, work or language.

sections.heading: Follow-up and warning signs
paragraphs: Breathing difficulty, throat swelling or collapse after food is an emergency; use prescribed adrenaline immediately and call emergency services. Persistent diarrhea, weight loss or anemia need assessment, even without dramatic reactions.

examples.title: A practical example
examples.text: In this hypothetical example, Mira plans to remove gluten for bloating. She first discusses testing so the dietary change does not obscure a possible celiac diagnosis.

examples.title: Another practical example
examples.text: In this hypothetical example, Arben developed swelling after bread. He seeks allergy assessment rather than deliberately eating bread again to test a gluten theory.
